# Check authoring

The workflow for turning a checklist point into a real check, keeping the audit **deterministic** the whole way.

## 0. Dedup (always first)
Assess the point before writing anything:
- API: `POST /api/v1/checklist/assess` with `{ "point": "…" }`, or
- Python: `auditfast.services.intake_service.assess_point("…")`, or
- UI: the **Checklist** page.

If the result is `covered`, stop — run the existing check instead. If `not_covered`, the response includes a draft **proposal** (inferred pillar/scope/severity, a `@check` skeleton, and a remediation stub) to start from.

## 1. Research (read-only)
Use the `check-researcher` agent (or do it yourself):
- Confirm the data is fetchable today — search `fabric-skills/` and [docs/checks.md](../../../docs/checks.md), and the auditfast MCP catalog tools (`list_checks`, `describe_check`, `catalog_summary`).
- Pick **pillar · layer · scope · `requires[]`** and whether it is `automated` (verifiable now) or `roadmap` (needs an API the provider does not yet call).

## 2. Implement
Use the `check-implementer` agent:
- Add the `@check(...)` to `backend/src/auditfast/core/check/<pillar>/<layer>/automated.py`.
- Build the verdict with `core/check/helpers.py` — `binary` / `covered` / `graded` / `note` / `not_applicable`.
- **Return `not_applicable(...)` when the `requires` data is unavailable — never FAIL.**
- Assign the next `ref`; add its remediation text to `backend/config/remediation.yaml`.

## 3. Validate
Use the `check-reviewer` agent and the harness ([../harness/README.md](../harness/README.md)):
- `pytest -q`, `ruff check src`, registry-count sanity check.
- Update pinned counts in `tests/` (`test_api.py`, `conftest.py`, `test_engine.py`).

## Promoting a roadmap point
`roadmap.py` modules are generated by `build-manual-checks.py`. To promote a ref: write the evaluator in `automated.py`, add the ref to the `AUTOMATED` set in `build-manual-checks.py`, re-run it, add remediation, and re-pin the counts (AGENTS.md §6).

## Tools this skill relies on
- **fabric-skills/** — vendored `microsoft/skills-for-fabric` (Fabric REST + item semantics).
- **MCP** — see [../mcp/README.md](../mcp/README.md): the local `fabric-well-architected-auditor` server exposes the catalog and audit tools; hosted **FabricIQ** exposes read-only Power BI tools.
- **Agents** — `checklist-author` (orchestrator) → `check-researcher` → `check-implementer` → `check-reviewer`.
